text: What is Reichenbach's 'conjunctive fork,' and how did he use it to characterize the direction of time?
choices: A pair of simultaneous, independently sufficient causes of one effect, showing that the effect need not counterfactually depend on either cause
A trajectory that loops back through spacetime, correlating an event with its own causal past

A structure in which two correlated but separated events are explained by a common cause in their past rather than a common effect in their future — an asymmetry Reichenbach took to constitute the direction of time
A time-symmetric description in which advanced and retarded electromagnetic waves jointly determine radiation
explanation: Reichenbach's conjunctive fork is 'open' toward the future: correlations between separated events trace back to a common cause in the past, and this asymmetry, he argued, constitutes time's direction (the past is the direction of common causes). Option 0 describes causal overdetermination, option 1 describes a closed timelike curve, and option 3 describes the Wheeler-Feynman absorber theory — each a distinct notion from this unit.
